title: hotfix: legacy-client compatibility in SLO enforcer regional failover
author: Priya Menon
description:
Context: During a partial outage on 2026-02-24 we observed the SLO enforcer incorrectly triggering regional failover for a small subset of traffic originating from legacy clients that do not set the new 'X-RW-Client-Version' header. The enforcer state machine would mark a regional circuit as tripped, but legacy clients kept retrying in a tight loop which caused repeated back-pressure and prevented graceful recovery. This PR is a hotfix to make the SLO enforcer backward-compatible with legacy clients while preserving the stricter behavior for modern clients.

What this change does: 1) Adds a compatibility short-circuit for requests missing 'X-RW-Client-Version' so they follow an exponential backoff path that cooperates with the regional circuit-breaker instead of immediate retry loops. 2) Fixes a race in the circuit-breaker state transitions where a concurrent check + reset could cause the breaker to remain closed despite hit counts exceeding threshold. The fix introduces an atomic compare-and-swap transition and a small windowed counter to avoid stomping resets during flips. 3) Introduces a feature-flag 'slo.enforcer.legacy_backoff' (default: enabled for all regions for now) so we can roll back quickly if unintended. 4) Adds metrics and tracing spans to track legacy_client_backoff_rate, cb_state_transitions, and legacy_retry_loop_detection. 5) Adds unit + integration tests simulating legacy client behavior and a small e2e scenario that reproduces the original incident in the perf-canary harness.

Why this is a hotfix: The current behavior caused prolonged degradation for customers behind legacy client versions and interfered with regional failover smoothing. The change is narrowly scoped, guarded by a feature flag, and aims for minimal surface area in the runtime hot path.

Testing and rollout: - Unit tests covering state machine races and header-path. - Integration test injected into perf-canary which reproduces the legacy retry pattern; green on my local canary run and CI after a single rerun. - Deployed as a canary to us-west-2 (10% traffic) for 6 hours, monitored cb_state_transitions, request success rates, and the new legacy_client_backoff_rate metric. - After observing expected behavior, rollout to 50% and then 100% across regions.

Checklist: - [x] Add compatibility short-circuit for missing header - [x] Fix compare-and-swap race in circuit breaker - [x] Add metrics and tracing spans - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Canary rollout and monitoring - [x] Docs note in observability-pack about new metrics

Notes: The feature flag allows immediate rollback. I verified no notable latency regression for modern clients (<1ms p50 on the hot path). This PR touches the enforcement path and the routing logic; reviewers should pay attention to the atomic transition code in enforcer/circuit_breaker.go and the added test harness in perf-canary/replays/legacy-client.yaml.

review_comments: Ethan Caldwell: Can we make the feature flag default-off in production to be extra safe? If we ship default-on we should have a clear rollback playbook.

Priya Menon (author): We ran the canary with default-on in us-west-2 for 6 hours and saw stable recovery; I'm keeping default-on to fix customer-facing regressions quickly. Rollback steps are documented and flag supports immediate disable.
Mariana Lopes: The compare-and-swap logic looks correct, but add a comment clarifying why we use a windowed counter vs simple reset to avoid future regressions.
Priya Menon (author): Added comment and expanded unit test to assert behavior across concurrent flips.
Samir Patel: CI flaky failed once on perf-canary; re-run passed. Approving post-rerun.
Ethan Caldwell: Approved after confirming metrics names and dashboards were updated.
release_notes: Hotfix: Ensure legacy clients participate in exponential backoff during SLO enforcer regional failover; fix circuit-breaker state race. Adds feature-flag 'slo.enforcer.legacy_backoff' and new metrics: legacy_client_backoff_rate, cb_state_transitions.
